cards.back: Give each person the same amount. Share 10 sweets between 2 children: 5 each.
cards.say: Share equally. Give each person the same amount. Share ten sweets between two children: five each.

cards.back: To share or group equally. The sign is ÷. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
cards.say: Divide. To share or group equally. Twelve divided by two equals six.

cards.back: Putting things into equal groups. 12 apples in groups of 4 make 3 groups.
cards.say: Grouping. Putting things into equal groups. Twelve apples in groups of four make three groups.

cards.back: What is left over when you cannot share equally. 7 shared between 2 is 3 with 1 left over.
cards.say: Remainder. What is left over when you cannot share equally. Seven shared between two is three with one left over.

Fourteen divided by two equals seven. Seven times two equals fourteen.
Sixteen divided by two equals eight. Eight times two equals sixteen.
Eighteen divided by two equals nine. Nine times two equals eighteen.
Twenty divided by two equals ten. Ten times two equals twenty.
Twenty divided by ten equals two. Two times ten equals twenty.
Forty divided by ten equals four. Four times ten equals forty.
Seventy divided by ten equals seven. Seven times ten equals seventy.
Ninety divided by ten equals nine. Nine times ten equals ninety.
Twenty-five divided by five equals five. Five times five equals twenty-five.
Thirty divided by five equals six. Six times five equals thirty.
Forty-five divided by five equals nine. Nine times five equals forty-five.
Share eighteen stickers equally between two friends. Nine each. Eighteen divided by two equals nine.

cards.front: 20 children make groups of 5. How many groups?
cards.say: Twenty children make groups of five. How many groups? Four groups. Twenty divided by five equals four.

cards.front: 30 pencils in boxes of 10. How many boxes?
cards.say: Thirty pencils in boxes of ten. How many boxes? Three boxes. Thirty divided by ten equals three.

cards.front: 15 sweets are shared equally between 2 children. How many does each get, and how many are left over?
cards.say: Fifteen sweets are shared equally between two children. How many does each get, and how many are left over? Seven each and one sweet left over.

cards.back: No. 9 is odd, so 1 is left over.
cards.say: Can nine be shared equally between two? No. Nine is odd, so one is left over.
Division is the opposite of multiplication. If four times five equals twenty then twenty divided by five equals four.

cards.front: Half of 16 is the same as 16 ÷ ?
cards.say: Half of sixteen is the same as sixteen divided by what? Two. Halving is dividing by two.
Twenty-four divided by two equals twelve. Twelve plus twelve equals twenty-four.
